key_entities: plan-review criteria E4 T2 T3 T5b
propositions: A primary comment dedup guard that returns silently on guard conditions never populated its backing map (comment_ids) in production, despite 2475 bindings entries, because the ACLI batch mutation envelope lacks a top-level id field (GUARD 3 fires unconditionally).

The guard's failure was never detected because a secondary body-equality dedup fallback absorbed enough traffic to mask total primary-path failure as content-shape-correlated degradation (short comments deduped; formatted ones did not).

Test suite layers seed each other's invariants (apply tests use synthetic id-bearing payloads; differ tests use stub binding stores) but no test crosses the seam between them, so no test could observe that the real transport never delivers the id the apply layer expects.
Multiple review criteria (E4 external facts, T3 endpoint existence, T5b plan-level reliability) have scope boundaries that stop just short of silently-inert guards on correctness-critical paths.
The escape window was 6 days (feature launch to fix), not months, but the duplicate symptom it enabled persisted across 29931 comment duplicates until separate remediation.
A production observability signal (invariant alert on comment_ids remaining empty while outbound posts succeed) could have surfaced this inert guard at operation time with no CI coupling.
